I am organizing my research on federated learning and need to set up a knowledge base. Please search for papers about federated learning from the academic literature repository and organize them in two ways.

First, create a page in the team knowledge base titled "Federated Learning Research Hub". Inside this page, create a child database called "Paper Index" that contains an entry for each federated learning paper. Each entry should include the paper title, authors, and a short summary.

Second, create an Excel file called "Federated_Learning_Papers.xlsx" in my workspace. It should have two sheets. The first sheet "Paper Details" should have columns Paper_ID, Title, Authors, Year, and Abstract_Length (the character count of the abstract). The second sheet "Summary" should have columns Metric and Value, listing Total_Papers (the number of papers found), Avg_Abstract_Length (the average character count of all abstracts rounded to the nearest integer), Earliest_Year, and Latest_Year.

Please include all papers that are related to federated learning, including foundational papers about federated approaches and surveys of the field.

Note on the spreadsheet: write all numeric values (Abstract_Length and every Summary metric) as literal numbers in the cells. Do not rely on Excel formulas for these values, since formulas are not computed by the reading tool. Compute the values yourself (e.g. with your code tool) and fill in the resulting numbers.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, follow this exact orchestration plan. A wave must finish and return all stated handoffs before the next wave begins. Within a wave, dispatch exactly one sub-agent for each numbered sub-task and run those sub-agents concurrently.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 sub-agent for the following numbered sub-task:

   1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): Use one explore sub-agent to own complete read-only paper discovery. Issue complementary task-derived federated-learning queries to the local arXiv search at its supported per-call result bound, union and deduplicate the returned records by stable ID, and retain every genuinely relevant result including foundational and survey work. Because the search exposes no cursor or list-all operation, do not claim coverage beyond this observed query union. Preserve full title, complete authors, abstract, published date/year, and abstract character count, and return the normalized union directly with per-query/union/retained counts, IDs, year range, and abstract-length controls. Explore is read-only, so do not write files or create Notion or Excel state.

After Wave 1, the main agent must verify the complementary-query controls and deduplicated observed union, determine the related-paper count only from returned records, and freeze literal summary metrics and one title/author/summary record per retained paper using only task-visible runtime evidence.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

   1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own the Notion hierarchy exclusively. Search for an existing Federated Learning Research Hub, create at most one parent page, then create exactly one Paper Index child database under that returned parent and add one entry per frozen paper with title, authors, and a source-faithful short summary. Keep the whole create-parent → create-database → populate → read-back sequence in this agent. Return page/database IDs, entry count, covered IDs/titles, and validation. Do not write Excel.

   2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own Federated_Learning_Papers.xlsx exclusively. Create exactly Paper Details and Summary with the exact required headers, one row per frozen paper, literal numeric abstract lengths and metrics, and the rounded average, earliest year, and latest year. Read back both sheets and return path, row counts, summary values, and header/value validation. Do not modify Notion.

After Wave 2, the main agent must reconcile paper IDs, counts, authors, and summary metrics across the Notion database and workbook, verify both external state and file integrity, and then complete without adding unrelated papers or extra deliverables.

nodes.text:
You are creating a Notion knowledge-base structure for a researcher's federated learning literature collection. This is the ONLY external write you need to perform; do not create anything else.

CONTEXT
- The Notion workspace reachable by your integration token is currently EMPTY (a search with an empty query returns 0 results). There is no pre-existing "team knowledge base" page shared with the integration, so treat the workspace top level as the team knowledge base.
- Paper data below was gathered from the arXiv literature repository and is authoritative — use it exactly as given (do not invent or alter titles/authors).

DELIVERABLE 1 — Page
Create a top-level page (parent: {"workspace": true, "type": "workspace"}) titled exactly: Federated Learning Research Hub
Add an icon (e.g. 📚) if convenient, and append a single short intro paragraph as a content block, e.g.:
"Curated index of federated learning papers from the arXiv literature repository, including foundational work on federated optimization and surveys of the field."
Return the new page ID.

DELIVERABLE 2 — Child database
Inside that page, create a child database titled exactly: Paper Index
Schema (three properties):
- "Title"  : title
- "Authors": rich_text
- "Summary": rich_text
Then add one entry (row) per paper below with exactly these values:

1) Title: Communication-Efficient Learning of Deep Networks from Decentralized Data
   Authors: H. Brendan McMahan, Eider Moore, Daniel Ramage, Seth Hampson, Blaise Agüera y Arcas
   Summary: Foundational paper that coined the term Federated Learning: it trains deep networks on decentralized mobile-device data by aggregating locally-computed updates through iterative model averaging (FedAvg), and shows robustness to unbalanced, non-IID data with 10-100x fewer communication rounds than synchronized SGD.

2) Title: Federated Optimization in Heterogeneous Networks
   Authors: Tian Li, Anit Kumar Sahu, Manzil Zaheer, Maziar Sanjabi, Ameet Talwalkar, Virginia Smith
   Summary: Proposes FedProx, a re-parametrization of FedAvg that adds a proximal term to the local subproblem, and provides convergence guarantees plus more robust and fair convergence behavior across heterogeneous federated datasets.

3) Title: Federated Learning: Challenges, Methods, and Future Directions
   Authors: Tian Li, Anit Kumar Sahu, Ameet Talwalkar, Virginia Smith
   Summary: Survey of the unique characteristics and challenges of federated learning spanning distributed optimization, systems design, and statistical learning, with a broad overview of current approaches and directions for future work.

4) Title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
   Authors: Peter Kairouz, H. Brendan McMahan, Brendan Avent, Aurélien Bellet, Mehdi Bennis
   Summary: Survey covering recent advances in federated learning, where many clients collaboratively train a model orchestrated by a central server while keeping training data decentralized, and presenting an extensive collection of open problems and challenges.

NOTES / GOTCHAS
- The database must be a CHILD of the "Federated Learning Research Hub" page (parent page_id = the page you created), not a standalone database, and it must be a real database object (not just a table of text blocks).
- Use the Notion MCP tools only (search, post-page, create-a-database, post-database-query, patch-block-children, retrieve-*).
- If creating a workspace-level page fails, fall back to searching for any existing top-level page (query "Research" or similar) and use it as parent; report what you did.
- Do not archive or delete anything.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA / REPORT BACK
Report: (a) the created page ID and URL, (b) the created database ID, (c) confirmation that all 4 rows exist with the exact title/authors/summary values (e.g. by querying the database back), and (d) any deviations. Do not claim success unless the page, the child database, and all 4 entries are verifiably present.
Create Notion FL research hub

Build a local Excel workbook with the exact specifications below. This is your only deliverable.

FILE PATH (create exactly this file):
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-federated-learning-notion/workspace/Federated_Learning_Papers.xlsx

CRITICAL RULE: every numeric cell must be a LITERAL number written into the cell — no Excel formulas at all (no =LEN(...), =COUNTA(...), =AVERAGE(...), etc.). A downstream reader reads cached cell values only and cannot evaluate formulas. All values below are already computed for you.

The workbook must contain exactly two sheets.

SHEET 1 — name: "Paper Details"
Header row in A1:E1: Paper_ID, Title, Authors, Year, Abstract_Length
Then these 4 data rows (in this order):

Paper_ID: 1602.05629 | Title: Communication-Efficient Learning of Deep Networks from Decentralized Data | Authors: H. Brendan McMahan, Eider Moore, Daniel Ramage, Seth Hampson, Blaise Agüera y Arcas | Year: 2016 | Abstract_Length: 1230

Paper_ID: 1812.06127 | Title: Federated Optimization in Heterogeneous Networks | Authors: Tian Li, Anit Kumar Sahu, Manzil Zaheer, Maziar Sanjabi, Ameet Talwalkar, Virginia Smith | Year: 2018 | Abstract_Length: 744

Paper_ID: 1908.07873 | Title: Federated Learning: Challenges, Methods, and Future Directions | Authors: Tian Li, Anit Kumar Sahu, Ameet Talwalkar, Virginia Smith | Year: 2019 | Abstract_Length: 601

Paper_ID: 1912.04977 | Title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning | Authors: Peter Kairouz, H. Brendan McMahan, Brendan Avent, Aurélien Bellet, Mehdi Bennis | Year: 2019 | Abstract_Length: 642

Year and Abstract_Length must be stored as numbers (integers), not text strings.

SHEET 2 — name: "Summary"
Header row in A1:B1: Metric, Value
Then these 4 data rows:
- Total_Papers | 4
- Avg_Abstract_Length | 804
- Earliest_Year | 2016
- Latest_Year | 2019
All four Value cells must be literal numbers.

Formatting: make the header rows bold and freeze the top row if convenient — cosmetic only, data correctness is what matters. Do not add extra columns (no computed columns), no extra sheets.

TOOLS: use the Excel MCP tools (create_workbook / create_worksheet / write_data_to_excel / format_range etc.). If the default new workbook already contains a sheet (e.g. "Sheet"), rename or delete it so the final file has exactly the two required sheets named exactly "Paper Details" and "Summary".

VERIFY BEFORE REPORTING: read back both sheets with the Excel read tool and confirm the header names, sheet names, and every cell value match the spec exactly, and that all numbers are stored as numbers. Report the final file path, the sheet names, and the read-back content (values only) as confirmation. Do not claim success if any cell is wrong or if any formula was used.
